title: A replace ref under refs/replace could change the blobs or the commit tree that status and snapshot read
resolution: GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 joins the built environment and contract section 7; tests replace a blob and the head commit.

title: An assume-unchanged or skip-worktree index flag hid a modified tracked file, so remove could delete unpublished work
resolution: Status first clears both flags through ls-files -v and update-index; contract section 6 says so; one test per flag.

title: Standard output of a process that carries the credential was returned without scrubbing
resolution: Standard output of a process with a credential is scrubbed byte-preserving; a test echoes the header on both streams.

title: Credential forms shorter than eight characters were not redacted, because the runner used the conformance heuristic
resolution: The runner redacts every non-empty form through its own credentialForms; a test with a three-character secret.

title: Node added NODE_V8_COVERAGE to the Git environment, and only the tests removed it
resolution: The runner names NODE_V8_COVERAGE as undefined so Node leaves it out; the tests no longer withhold it and a runner test sets it.

title: The checkout walk decoded names as UTF-8, so a directory whose name is not UTF-8 made the operation reject with ENOENT
resolution: The walk reads names and builds paths as bytes; tests cover a committed file and a gitfile under such a directory.

title: File system errors escaped prepare, inspect, snapshot, and remove as rejected promises
resolution: System errors become unavailable at the boundary, a malformed record internal, a crash still rejects; fault-injection tests.

title: A failed revision lookup read as a missing revision, so a prepare could fall back to the base branch
resolution: The lookup returns Result of string or undefined, with only exit code 1 as missing; a test fails rev-parse with exit 128.

title: The cat-file reader accepted another object type, a negative size, and objects that were not requested
resolution: The reader requires the requested blobs in order with a strict header, enough bytes, and nothing after; negative tests.

title: The status parser accepted malformed fields and output without the branch headers
resolution: Every field, path, and the branch.oid and branch.head headers are validated; negative tests per field.

title: The tree listing accepted a mode with trailing characters and an empty path
resolution: The mode must be six octal digits and the path non-empty; negative tests.

title: A gitlink added only to the index hid a directory of work from inspect and remove
resolution: Inspect compares the merged index entries, gitlinks included, with the verified head tree and reports modified on any difference; contract section 6; scenario Change hidden by the index; test a gitlink added only to the index never hides a directory of work.

title: Forged stat data in the index hid a modified tracked file of the same size
resolution: Inspect writes every index entry anew with git update-index -z --index-info from git ls-files --stage -z, so no stat data, flag, or cache tree survives; contract section 6; test forged stat data in the index never hides a modified tracked file.

title: A forged cache tree in the index hid a staged change
resolution: The index rebuild invalidates the cache tree and the merged index is compared with the verified head tree; test a forged cache tree never hides a staged change.

title: Objects read for the snapshot and the head tree were not checked against their names, so a forged pack or commit-graph changed what was read
resolution: Cat-file --batch reads the commit, trees, and blobs, each must hash to its name, else internal; core.commitGraph and core.multiPackIndex off; contract sections 7 and 10; tests an object whose bytes do not hash to its name fails the snapshot, a forged commit-graph never changes what status reads.

title: A FIFO, socket, or device in the Git directory was accepted and could block a Git process
resolution: The Git directory may hold only directories and regular files, anything else is unsafe-checkout; contract section 7; tests a FIFO as .git/index, a FIFO deeper in .git.

title: Tree paths that Git refuses, such as .., .git, or a duplicate name, reached the snapshot
resolution: New reason unsafe-tree-path (isSafeTreeName, after Git's verify_path); snapshotTree and encodeHeadSnapshot refuse such names, duplicates, and a file that is also a directory; contract 9 and 10; design D16; test a path that Git refuses, or a file that is also a directory, is refused.

title: The failure table of contract section 9 lacked unavailable for file system faults and internal for malformed records or Git output
resolution: Section 9 extends the unavailable row with file system faults and adds an internal row for a malformed record, unreadable Git output, an object that does not hash to its name, or a failed Git process; coordinator decision M3 in design.

title: Any lstat error read as absence, so an unreadable record or marker looked absent
resolution: entryAt and isPresent treat only ENOENT and ENOTDIR as absent and reject on any other error, which becomes unavailable; test a file system error other than absence rejects instead of reading as unsafe.

title: VerifiedGitClient was structural, so an object literal passed for a verified client
resolution: The class holds a private #verified field, making it nominal; type test with @ts-expect-error in only the gate makes a verified client, also for the type checker.

title: Prepare left the staging entry after a non-crash failure of the rename and did not define a failure after it
resolution: Prepare deletes the staging entry after a failure before the rename; one after it is unavailable and keeps the workspace (contract 3); tests a file system fault at the rename into place leaves no staging entry, a fault after the rename into place fails the prepare and keeps the ready workspace.

title: The nested Git directory check compared .git case-sensitively
resolution: An entry named .git in any case is refused below the top and at the top unless it is .git itself; tests a nested Git directory in another case, a second Git directory in another case at the top.

title: The proposal was stale: stdout scrubbing, two added and two modified requirements, and the command-scope settings were missing
resolution: The proposal lists both scrubbed streams, every added and modified requirement, the new settings, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS, the reason unsafe-tree-path, and the amended contract sections.

title: The head tree listing dropped directory entries before the path check, so a refused or duplicate directory name reached the snapshot
resolution: readHeadTree keeps directory entries; snapshotTree checks their names and paths with the files, so a refused name, a name twice in one tree, or a file that is also a directory is unsafe-tree-path; tests through readHeadTree and snapshot.
